questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had dreamed of going to Italy for a long time, since I am really interested in Italian culture and language. I had Italian as my third language in high school, and also really wanted to improve my skills in this language. So it was also a personal connection that drew me to the destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the information I needed was sent to my e-mail by the exchange office from UCPH or my host institution, or otherwise it was available on the Unimi-website. If I had any questions I e-mailed my sending or host institution, and they were always very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received an e-mail telling us to go to the exchange office to get our proof of attendance document signed, and emails about how to register to courses, which was helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I know a lot of people who used different rental websites, and they all had good experiences even though they hadn't seen the apartments before arriving - the only thing about this is that it is very expensive (appr. 7000 pr person). My friend and I found housing via Airbnb, which was a bit cheaper since we chose to live together with one bedroom. I can really recommend this solution if you are going away with a close friend and don't mind sharing a bed with them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a big city, so if possible try to find an apartment that is close to a metro line, which will make it easier to get to campus. Or if possible, try to find an apartment that is close to the campus. This was difficult for us since we only found the exact location of the classes after registering for the classes, and the location varied between classes. We lived in an area called Washington, which was a really nice and calm/residential area, and had a metro that went straight to campus, other nice areas to live in could be Porta Venezia, Porta Romana or Città Studi.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were clear guidelines for how to register in the e-mails, and you could also try different classes before registering in order to be sure which classes you were interested in attending, so it was quite flexible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guidelines from the host institution.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, we got all the courses we wanted and were locky that their schedules didn't overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Since many of our courses were mandatory, we didn't have as much freedom in choosing which ones we wanted to attend. So some of our mandatory courses found place at a really annoying time during the day (from 3-6 p.m., four times a week). If I could have chosen freely, I would have chosen classes that had a good schedule instead of the content of the courses, since being on exchange for me was more about exploring the city and making friends than the courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Even though the courses were MA, the level was much lower than the bachelors courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not quite good; 1,5 hour long classes with no breaks, where the teacher talked and talked during the whole class with very few class discussions and group work. It was really hard for me to concentrate and to be sure of what I was expected to learn from the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Research Methods in Social and Political Science
Employment, Inequalities and Discrimination in the Global Labour Market
Human Resources Management
Conflict Management and Negotiation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you study psychology and are on exchange during the 5th semester of your bachelor's programme, I would recommend all of these courses together, since they were the only ones that didn't overlap in the schedule, and since the are approved as the mandatory courses you are supposed to have during the 5th semester at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: During the first month, there were a few unexpected costs in getting our apartment ready such as extension cords, storage for the bathroom and an extra chair.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I used more money than I expected on traveling around the country and visiting many different cities, however this was very well-spent money that resulted in amazing experiences that I wouldn't have been without. Going out to dinner was less expensive than I expected; we found many places that served amazing food at really good prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really use the non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could be a member of the Erasmus network (ESN), where there were different trips, walks around the city and sometimes parties you could participate in. I was a member, but very rarely used the offers.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend traveling around the country, walking around the city and enjoy the parks, architecture, museums, restaurants and bars.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend traveling to different cities in Italy and seeing how they differ according to their geographical location. It can also just be a day trip, it doesn't have to be a long holiday. My biggest recommendations are Venice, Verona, Bologna, Rome and Naples, and if possible, go with some of your new friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, I didn't find Milan that different from Copenhagen. If you like Italian culture, then you will find it nice adjusting to the culture:)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it quite hard to socialize with the students from my class, since there were very few class discussions and group work, and since the classes I attended were second year masters courses, so the other students seemed to be quite established in who they were friends with. We ended up going on a trip to Verona with some people from our class during the end of the semester, which was really fun. I really wanted to make a local friend, so I ended up downloading an app called Bumble and going on some friend-dates, which I would really recommend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes understanding the Italian-English accent.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The vibe in the city, people really using the city; there were always kids playing in the park, many people sitting at bars and cafés. I really appreciated going to trattorias, enjoying the weather, drinking negronis.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about the exams, don't have too many guests from home/don't go home too often while you are there; it will go by so fast, so enjoy it while it lasts and enjoy your free time, and go to as many bars and restaurants as you want (enjoy that it is much cheaper to do this than in Copenhagen).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding feeling was meeting many new people, especially people from my own campus and study field at UCPH, which I would have never met if not on exchange. It was also really rewarding challenging myself to live in a new city, and quickly feeling like it was my home. And also the academic level being much lower than at UCPH; it was really rewarding having more free time and being able to go to so many different cities and feeling free to do this without worrying about school.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not worrying too much about the exams and not being sure what I was expected to learn from the classes; looking back, I would have spent much less time on school, since the exams ended up being quite a lot easier than expected. And another great challenge was missing my friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
